So rather than enter into an academic discussion, I think we will watch what does happen. If Mr. Stamp errs, between us we will stop him, Mr. Djurdjic. Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is the interview of Mr. Stevanovic on the 10th of August, 2002. If we could go to page 19 in the English, line 23. Well, just page 19 in the English. If we could see the area around line 23. And that is page 26 in B/C/S. While we're getting there, you said, Mr. Djordjevic, and this is at page 9413 of the transcript, that once Mr. Stojiljkovic was appointed, you never held a single collegium on your own of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Maybe I misunderstood.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we scroll down the English transcript, please. Your Honours, I wonder if this might be a convenient time, because I notice that the -- the page references are not entirely correct, so maybe I could check that in the break so we could move more speedily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Good move, Mr. Stamp. We will adjourn now. We will resume in one hour's time, having had the lunch break. So we now adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic, were there meetings of the collegium, the ministers' collegium, during 1998?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And were there meetings of the ministers' collegium during 1999 as well?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You said earlier, and this is page 9413 of the transcript, from line 5, which is what I quoted to you immediately before the break but I'll just read it again: "When Minister Stojiljkovic became minister, I was acting chief of the RJB, and later on in 1998 when I became chief of RJB, I never held a single collegium of mine own. That is to say there was no collegium of the public security. The minister of interior once a week inquired of his collegium all the heads of the different lines of work in the headquarters of the ministry, that is to say all the heads of administrations then he called the chief of the secretariat of internal affairs in Belgrade and all the assistant ministers in the ministry." If we could look at this document again. This is the record of Mr. Stevanovic's interview, and we want page 20, line 1 in English, page 26, line 24 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, sir. What you have read out is false. I don't know what kind of translation this is, but the first sentence about Minister Stojiljkovic and of me being head of public security and all that, these are not my words. I never said that. I really don't understand how these transcripts are made. I can say how it should be. I wasn't chief when the minister arrived or anything. I really don't understand how things are recorded here. But I can explain everything from the beginning if necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to focus on the collegium for the time being. While Minister Stojiljkovic was minister, you didn't hold any of your own collegium. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The deputy minister and the chief of public security who was the highest-ranking official in the ministry was killed on the 11th of April, 1997. At that moment, I was the highest-ranking colonel-general, and I was assistant minister. Mirko Marjanovic, the prime minister, who was responsible for the ministry said to me, "There is no minister. You are the highest-ranking official. Until we resolve the situation you will be in charge of the ministry." After some days -- ten days or so Minister Stojiljkovic arrived, and during that time I continued as was earlier done by the chief of sector, and when Minister Stojiljkovic arrived he said to me, "Continue the way you worked before," and that went on until the 1st of June. And so only on the 1st of June did I become acting official, and then he appointed the assistants. And after that only one collegium was held with the minister, and -- who was present and who had briefings is mentioned there, and then we also saw the document, the official document by which he called his collegium in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. I'm trying to move quickly, so I'll just ask you, you also -- there were also collegium meetings in 1999, meetings of the ministers' collegium.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was our usual way of work.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Throughout the war as well?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, throughout the war. If sometimes a situation was critical, we may have failed to meet, but as a rule it went on throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And it was approximately -- it was usually once a week?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Usually on Tuesdays?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as far as I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And Mr. Stevanovic said this: "He said once a week the minister held his collegium but not often this was done on his behalf by the head of the service, the public security service. As far as I remember, this was always on a Tuesday." Do you recall holding the collegium meetings on behalf of the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what that is supposed to mean, a collegium meeting on behalf of the minister. There was no such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall holding or chairing collegium meetings in the absence of the minister? And let's focus on 1999 -- in 1999.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me first tell you I never chaired the collegium for the minister in his presence [as interpreted]. There was no such situation. And now we can focus on whichever year you prefer.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: "In his absence," not "in the minister's presence."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we find the corresponding page in B/C/S, the one we have here? We're looking at page 20 in English. I think we want page 26 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There's a mistake in the transcript on line 22. It should read, "In the absence," and not "in the presence."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's corrected at lines 24 and 25.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could you go in B/C/S to page 26, and could we view line 14 -- line 24. We're on page 27 now, I think. Oh, it's page 27 it's actually I'm told. Mr. Stevanovic is recorded to have said here: "More often -- I'll just read the whole sentence. "Once a week the minister held his collegium but more often this was done on his behalf by the head of service, the public security service." Do you recall that? Do you recall that you often held these collegium meetings on behalf of the minister?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just said I held collegiums from the 11th of April for the month that followed until the minister settled the personnel issues and until he drafted a decision by which he appointed me acting official, and which meeting Stevanovic is referring to here I really don't know. The minister never entrusted me to chair a meeting attended by all assistants or people from the state security or anything else. He may be referring to meetings before the minister resolved these issues. Then they were at meetings with me. But that was up until the -- until mid-1997. After that, the minister took over these duties and it -- it wasn't possible for me to chair meetings on his behalf.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In any case, these meetings would involve the minister, yourself, the heads of the different lines of work in headquarters, that is the heads of the administrations, and the chief of the secretariat for Belgrade, as well as the assistant ministers. Are those the regular attendees at these collegium meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and apart from these you mentioned, there was also the chief of state security and his assistant minister. Yes, there were such meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And if we could move on to page 46 in English. We want to look in the vicinity of line 5. And page 63 in Serbian, starting from line 1. At these collegium meetings, particularly in 1999, wasn't the security in Kosovo always the focus of attention? Was this one of the main topics on the agenda of these collegium meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That wasn't the main topic at all. The topic was general security. If we're referring to 1999. If we're talking about 1998. So if we focus on 1999, I can speak my mind, but I don't know which year you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Let's focus on 1998 first. Was one of the main topics on the agenda for discussion in 1998 the security situation in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When the situation in Kosovo was most complicated I was in Kosovo, so I didn't attend these collegium meetings. I suppose that they also spoke about the security situation in Kosovo, but I wasn't present and cannot comment. In 1998, when it -- when the situation was most difficult, I was down there all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In 1999, was the security situation in Kosovo also an important topic on the agenda of these collegium meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1999, since the start of the bombing, the main topic was not only Kosovo, it was the general situation in Serbia. And as for Kosovo, the chiefs of the administrations, we saw some minutes of other meetings. So these chiefs and the -- they only briefed about logistical issues and problems if there were any. At collegium meetings, there was no discussion about combat activities involving the units deployed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And could we look at line 46 -- sorry, line 26 in the English. Page 47, line 26. And if we could find the corresponding part. Did you discuss tactics for the forces to employ or that could be employed by the forces in Kosovo during the collegium meetings in 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to know whether Obrad Stevanovic is speaking about meetings held in 1998 or 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, that's -- we'll get to that. Focus on my question. Did you discuss tactics in respect to the tactics that could be employed by the members of the MUP in Kosovo in 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for the carrying out of anti-terrorist activities in Kosovo or for the defence of the country in that territory the minister established a MUP staff, the headquarters of which was in Pristina. The MUP staff had its personnel responsible for individual areas including the entire activities there. And the actions and operations down there they both planned and carried out in co-ordination with the military. At the ministers' collegium meetings, there was never any discussion about operations conducted by units in Kosovo. That was the staff's responsibility within -- it was within their remit. And the way Obrad is discussing it here, well, that's a discussion at a very general level about some security situation and some general tasks, what happened during the bombing, but -- or rather during the bombings Obrad didn't attend these meeting because he was in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you discuss at the meetings in 1999, particularly in February of 1999, the plans for the upcoming anti-terrorist offensive in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should we have discussed it? Who should have presented those plans when the -- all the experts were down in Kosovo? No -- no plans were discussed at this collegium meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Wasn't it -- well, were these -- were minutes taken of these meetings, the collegium meetings in 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you get copies? Weren't copies distributed to all participants in the meeting?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The copies -- or, rather, the minutes were taken by somebody from the analyses administration, and a day or two after the meeting there was a general summary of what was discussed there with the conclusions ordered by the minister, and that document was then distributed to all the persons that had attended the collegium meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know where the official minutes were supposed to be stored or what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that a set of minutes should certainly be stored with the analysis administration which originally drafted them. In addition to that, all the participants at the meetings had to have copies of them, but what became of these minutes is not something I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you keep copies?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throughout my time there copies were kept with the chef de cabinet. As soon as I received the document, I would review it and hand it over to be stored. On my retirement, I was no longer interested in that. I don't know where the minutes are held.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Wasn't it part of the rules of your service that you should keep a work notebook?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was never the case on the police force. This is typical for the army. The police never had such official documents as a notebook which had to be filled out and filed. Well, you see, Djakovic kept private notes which now carry the weight of evidence, but this wasn't typical of the police. Everyone had their own notebooks or notes, and it was their personal business as to what they did with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not Obrad Stevanovic kept a work notebook?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you see him take notes at meetings?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every participant at the collegium meeting carried along a notebook or --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- shuffle of papers that they would either make notes on or report from.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. Could we look at 01898. This is a handwritten notebook of -- of Mr. Stevanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think that the document which the Prosecutor seeks to present is a very specific one, and I'd like to provide some explanations. This is a document which the Prosecution sought to tender into evidence but withdrew the request once the Defence put forth their submissions, and this was supposed to be done through witness Philip Coo.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know if there is cause for us to move into private session, because I think some of the matters I wish to address now were discussed in private session in a different case before this Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, before we get into discussion, there are dangers with the accused here who must always be present in addressing upon matters which might turn out to be assisting in the answers. May I just say I merely want to show him what is recorded in the notebook and get his comments.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. We will proceed along that course without needing to hear your full submissions about this notebook, Mr. Djurdjic, because unless the witness adopts what's in this notebook it's -- it doesn't go any further with us. Carry on, Mr. Stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we just go to page 2 in the B/C/S. In the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This is Mr. Stevanovic's writing, Mr. Djordjevic? Can you identify it?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we go to page 40 and 41 in English. B/C/S, 29 to 30. Is that the corresponding page in B/C/S? In B/C/S is -- I think in B/C/S we might want to look at the preceding page.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: It is the corresponding page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay, could we go to the top of the page then, please. Could we scroll to the top of the page in English please. And could we get that part in B/C/S. 16th of February, 1999, collegium of the NRJB. Final meeting in Belgrade, Friday at something hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This writing is clearer now. Can you identify the writing, Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot, nor did there exist a collegium at the time. If this is to refer to a collegium of the chief of the public security sector, then I can tell you that there was no such collegium at that point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page in B/C/S. I want to find the part where it says "For the collegium of the minister."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I think it is referring there, Mr. Djordjevic, to a collegium of the minister. Do you recall a meeting being held, a collegium meeting of the minister, being held on the 16th of February? 1999.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First in relation to the previous sentence there is reference to a collegium of public security there. Is the author of these notes a member of the collegium? That's the basic question. And who does this notebook belong to? So if Obrad was supposed to be a member of my collegium, that doesn't make sense to me, because an assistant minister cannot be a member of the collegium of an assistant minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But just --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This really isn't clear to me at all who was writing and what that person was writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I'm instructed that this is the notebook of Mr. Obrad Stevanovic. I have those clear instructions. He has [indiscernible] for the collegium of the minister, and he also dates it, which is coming back to the question, and I remind you we don't have much time, the 16th of February, 1999. Do you recall attending any collegium meeting on the 16th of February, 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall it. How should I recall a specific collegium meeting on a specific date ten years later to this day? I don't deny that a collegium of ministers was held that week. We would normally have collegium meetings on Tuesdays every week, but whether one was held on the 16th of February is really beyond me. I cannot possibly recall everything. I can't recall what the discussions were about or who kept notes of the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, you recall just about that period having discussions at a collegium meeting where the finishing touches of a plan for a broad anti-terrorist operation with the MUP and the Pristina Corps was discussed?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where are you reading this from? Where am I supposed to find it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: It's just the first starred item under item 1. "Together with the Pristina Corps, the finishing touches are being put to a plan for a broad anti-terrorist operation in the period between the possible air-strikes and the entry of ground forces." Do you remember that discussion?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly, this is preparation for discussion. It doesn't mean that he presented these positions. He was merely preparing himself for the meeting. I am not familiar with this sort of thing at all, with this sort of topic being discussed at the collegium meeting. If this is indeed his notebook and the date, then he probably made note of something that he intended to discuss. Whether he actually talked about it is not something I can tell you now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: In the police administration, that's the next starred item: "... a plan is being prepared for measures to be taken in accordance with a plan of defence in case of possible NATO aggression." Do you recall that being discussed at collegium meetings in mid-February 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was reference to general preparations and updating all the defence plans within the ministry. This was the sort of orders that were issued at the time for the structures out in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And the next note, the next starred note is: "Preparations are also underway for your meeting with SUP chiefs and Department of Border Police commanders in Pristina, at 1100 hours on Wednesday." Now, I just inform you that the 16th of February, 1999, was a Tuesday. Do you remember briefings and -- well, before I even go on, do you recall that we discussed earlier on your presence and participation at a meeting in Pristina on the 17th, Wednesday the 17th of February, 1999? Do you recall at a meeting the day before that, a collegium on the Tuesday before that, you were briefed on preparations for a meeting with SUP chiefs and department of the border police in Pristina for the next day?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember at a collegium meeting the day before the meeting in Pristina on the 17th that it was discussed that you will also deliver decisions on early promotions to higher ranks, which is the next item?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the meeting held in the staff on the 17th of February I informed about it, but at this sort of meeting that discussed this sort of topic and this sort of an agenda, I think -- I'm not familiar with it. Now, in relation to the first items of the agenda, was this something that Obrad made note of that he intended to present to the minister? I really can't tell you. Those were his notes based on which he would probably address the minister, but I don't know what this is all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Well, can you recall being briefed that you would be -- deliver decisions on early promotions to higher ranks? And ...

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I did at the meeting on the following day, and that was the extent of my obligation which I discharged at the meeting on the following day. I didn't discuss anything else, either the terrorist or anti-terrorist activities or any other obligations that there may have existed at this meeting with the minister. I had my task. Assistant ministers who were responsible for certain other matters discussed different topics with the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes, but you don't seem to remember much about what was discussed. Do you remember, simply, do you remember, that before you went down to this big meeting in Pristina there was a collegium meeting the day before?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, how should I be able to remember ten years on? Do I remember when a meeting was held ten years ago, what the subjects discussed were, and who discussed them? Well, I simply don't know how I should remember that. If there were minutes reflecting the topics that were discussed, fine, but these were personal notes written by someone who may have intended to do this and that, and you're taking it as a conclusion that this was something that indeed transpired at the meeting. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honours, could this document be marked for the time being, for identity?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It can be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P1509 marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look again at P85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I complete what I was about to state and then we interrupted it? Let me inform Their Honours that this is a document -- may I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm not seeing the purpose of it at this moment, Mr. Djurdjic. We -- at the moment this document isn't going anywhere. We will see whether any more use is made of it, and it may or may not become useful to hear you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You look at the participants in that meeting, Mr. Djordjevic, and you see --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Also: "General Lukic opened the meeting devoted to the security situation and assigning future tasks." And you say, if we could go towards the bottom that General Lukic was discussing a plan of the RJB -- I'm quoting: "A plan of the RJB has been worked out to prevent and thwart the enemy of NATO troops into our territory. The staff plans, when it is ordered to carry out three mopping-up operations in the Podujevo, Dragobilje, and Drenica areas and has allotted around 4.000 policemen, etcetera, for that plan." Just take note of that for the time being. Could we move to the last page. Recorded here: "Colonel-General Vlastimir Djordjevic said that five officers from the AP, that's from Kosovo and Metohija, were awarding early promotions and had given them decisions on promotion." And having seen that, do you now recall that the day before this major meeting there was a collegium meeting in which these two matters were discussed?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: About the RJB plan, promotions, or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These two plans, the plans for the anti-terrorist mopping-up operation and the early award, the award of early promotion to some staff.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I can see here is my obligation, which I met, and I can only see it next to the promotion decision. Nowhere else do I see any obligations of mine arising from any of the plans in relation to any activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Was there also at that time, Mr. Djordjevic, a broader Serbia-wide plan that was being prepared, a defence plan that your ministry was involved in preparing?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly there existed a defence plan at the national level. That's customary for all. What I am not clear on is the role of the ministry. I know the obligations that I placed upon the secretariats and that was to update their own plans to update the system of mobilisation and calling up the reserve force, et cetera. Now, as for the plans for the defence of the country for the public security sector as to how to prevent NATO forces from entering the country, that's not something I'm aware of. That's not the sort of plan that public security would produce. There was a dispatch asking for the regular defence plans which any organisational unit of public security had to be updated and activated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: If we could go back to P -- sorry, to the document just marked for identity. That's P1509 just for the record. And could we just go to page -- page 4 of it. It's a little bit difficult to see, but could you scroll further to the right of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The question is -- just look at this, and can you tell us if this represents to your memory, and I know you probably couldn't be absolutely precise, but approximately the number of troops -- sorry, the number of policemen who were assigned and active in Kosovo in April 1999? The 3rd of April, 1999.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 3rd of April, 1999, I was charged with the secretariats outside of Kosovo and Metohija. All additional units that were deployed – the units from Kosovo and Metohija – were the responsibility of others. I'm really not familiar with this number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: That's all you need to say. So you're saying that notwithstanding that you're chief of the public security department, you didn't know approximately how many policemen were serving in Kosovo during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not, because it was the MUP staff in Kosovo that was responsible for all these forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: But headquarters would have to at least supply them with logistics. You signed the orders deploying PJP officers down there and withdrawing some on rotation. Are you saying that at your headquarters you had divested yourself of the policemen in Kosovo to such an extent that you would not -- could not give the Court an idea of how many police officers were stationed down there during the war?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this table is accurate. I don't know who made it or where the document is from, but it's possible that the figure is accurate. However, the tasks they carried out in Kosovo were not under my agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I…,I…,I…, you know-- [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My task --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: You know, you have said that many times. I'm not asking you about the tasks that you carried out. Prior to this period, in January 1999 did you attend a co-ordination meeting with Mr. Milosevic, Mr. Milutinovic, Mr. Ojdanic, Mr. Stojiljkovic, Pavkovic, Lukic in Beli Dvor in Belgrade, the 5th of January, 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have attended that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Without wasting time, I represent to you now that Mr. Sainovic, in his interview with the Prosecution, said that on that day there was a co-ordination meeting on Sainovic, the 5th of January, 1999 -- sorry, a co-ordination meeting on the situation in Kosovo on the 5th of January, 1999, which included Mr. Milutinovic, Mr. Milosevic, Mr. Ojdanic, Mr. Stojiljkovic, Mr. Pavkovic, and Mr. Lukic. Do you recall attending that meeting in your capacity as chief of the public security department?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We've had an answer to that. "I may have attended," was the witness's answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Your Honour, that is not a direct answer to my question. If he recalls attending or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He said, "I may have attended."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I heard him, but is that a direct answer whether he recalls --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that's all you're going to get, Mr. Stamp. I think you need to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you recall escorting Mr. Seselj down to Kosovo in mid-January 1999?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't escort Seselj in Kosovo. I was in the escort of the prime minister and the minister of the interior, and Seselj was there as vice-prime minister, and there were other vice-prime ministers. I believe there were four vice-prime ministers in all with the prime minister and other ministers.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we have a look at the video which is 65, 0980. Sorry, it is 65 ter number 0980.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "... parliament duly backed Milosevic's rejection of the Rambouillet terms as did the Serb public. Serbia's deputy prime minister revealed what Milosevic was planning to do next."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] If it comes to bombing by the NATO alliance, if an American aggression happens, we Serbs will suffer significant casualties, but there will be no Albanians in Kosovo."

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you. Could it be played again without any translation so the witness might hear in B/C/S what Mr. Seselj was saying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we haven't seen any date indication in this video. The OTP showed us a video, but we don't know when it -- when the footage was taken or where. So the OTP might as well inform us when this was shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The witness can be asked to provide that information. But it was in Belgrade in March 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Belgrade, March 1999, Mr. Djurdjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Do you remember -- could -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could this be played again but without the translation so the witness could hear it in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: "Serbia's parliament duly backed Milosevic's rejection of the Rambouillet terms as did the Serb public. Serbia's deputy prime minister revealed what Milosevic was planning to do next. "[No interpretation]"

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: This was, Mr. Djordjevic, in March after the Rambouillet talks broke down. Were -- were you aware of Mr. Seselj's pronouncements at this rally? This is a massive rally in Belgrade at a very critical period.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't really know anything about this rally of his, and he's well known for using every plight of the Serbian people for his own political benefit. He didn't give that speech as deputy prime minister. And this is the first time I've seen this. What he said over there and who was committed by it, that's part of Mr. Seselj's political story. He always had some comments of his own, but all were intended for his own personal promotion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. That went well beyond what I was asking. Weren't you aware at that time when you were planning for the defence of the country that there was a hardening of attitudes by some persons in the leadership of the country that involved the expulsion of the Kosovo Albanian population from Kosovo as a solution to the problems in Kosovo? Weren't you aware that many people in the leadership were expressing those views?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The man who put forward these positions hasn't set foot in Kosovo in 1999. So all his activity was words, words that committed nobody.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Weren't his White Eagles down there, his paramilitary down there, acting sometimes in concert with policemen?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of the White Eagles being his organisation. As far as my knowledge goes, no member of his party in whichever organisation was in Kosovo and Metohija, and he personally also never went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we move on to another document that was shown -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Before we move on, could this video be received in evidence and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P1510.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we look at D3232.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: These are the instructions on information and reporting. You spent a long time on it in chief in explaining the reporting system. Can you remind us, did the staff and the SUPs, were they supposed to send reports to -- to headquarters in Belgrade on the basis of these instructions?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And --

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The secretariats did, but this instruction didn't contain duties of the staff. This was a normal instruction about information and reporting, but it doesn't include the duties of the staff, only the duties of the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did the staff send its reports to Belgrade on the basis of this instruction, notwithstanding that the instruction did not include the staff?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In accordance with the elements as is set out here, they submitted reports for Belgrade because that was the format of the reports that they received from the secretariats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: When we speak of anti-terrorist operations, Mr. Djordjevic, these operations frequently would involve searches, raids, blockades, ambushes of terrorists and such like; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Terrorist ambushes, well, I don't know what to do with that phrase, whatever it means, but at any rate, if you're asking me whether this instruction obliged the staff to report about all this, then my answer is negative.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we go to page 3 in English, "Daily Reporting." That's the part under Roman numeral III, and I think perhaps it's the same page in the B/C/S. We'd like to scroll down to the bottom in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes. I think you will start reading those first two lines and then move to the next page only in B/C/S. When you're ready, say the word.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this urgent information from item 1 or daily information? What do you want me to read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no, you don't need to read it out. I just wanted you to refamiliarise yourself with the provisions in item 11. And you would need to go on the next page when you are finished with that.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now. What am I supposed to do with this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: No, no. I just wanted you to reorient yourself with this document. You remember you spend a long time on it when you testified in chief. It basically says here that the data that should be included in the daily reporting shall included -- shall include the data and events and developments included in the information and reporting list. And you were taken to the pages of the information and reporting list. I'd like to take you to the last page of it, because perhaps that one was missed. Just the last provision. If we could expand it in -- in Serbian, please. It says: "Operative actions and measures in which a large number of employees and materiel and equipment are engaged (searches, raids, blockades, searches of the terrain, ambushes, providing security and suchlike)." As one category of event that should be included in the daily reporting. The question now is this: Did you or anybody, to your knowledge, in the public security department instruct the SUPs not to include this type of data in their reports that they sent up on a daily basis?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This instruction includes events and developments in the regular implementation of duties and tasks. In the course of such implementation, what can happen is that some gang commits a crime and then a search is organised or ambushes are set up to catch them or in that sense some more complex activities, but this does not include anti-terrorist actions or other combat actions. So according -- this list isn't meant to apply to report about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So some --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I know you have your explanation, and perhaps that could come out again. I'm working against time. Just did you or anybody instruct the SUPs not to include this material in their reports?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No way. The secretariats were to report but about the events that I have mentioned, namely various more complex and yet regular activities involved in catching criminals and other bandits and so on, but not the way you want to interpreter it. Not what you want to read into it. Such cases are not included -- or, rather, this doesn't apply to such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's look at D296. These reports from the SUPs were supposed to include civilian casualties or crimes again civilians, weren't they? Mr. Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These reports must include crimes committed in the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The report on the 29th of March, 1999. And if you see the summary in the middle of the page it says: "... of security-related events, incidents, information registered between 600 hours on the 28th of March and 600 hours on the 29th of March, 1999." And this is from the MUP staff in Kosovo to the MUP Belgrade. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: The information I think you had said but remind me if I'm correct, the information contained in these reports would be similar to what would be contained in the reports that were sent up by the secretariats for the same period.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All information that the secretariats had and which are included in the list of that instruction, they were duty-bound to report to the staff and the ministry about it, because this -- these are regular activities and regular events that happened from 0 hours to 2400 hours. That's how it goes. And this report had an overview of security-related events. It is meant for regular events as covered by that instruction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Could we go to -- I think it's the last page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Under section for serious crimes there's nothing. It does not record any serious crimes. You will recall, Mr. Djordjevic, that at least to your certain knowledge in those hours in Podujevo there was a massacre of women and children that occurred -- that involved police members and occurred in the vicinity of the police station in Podujevo, according to Saranda Bogojevci who testified here?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Is there a reason why that crime, that serious crime, is not included in this report?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see a particular reason. That event was known, and the service took all measures from its remit with regard to that. Why it is not mentioned here I don't understand. The only explanation would be that what I said a little while ago is that this reporting covers regular or routine events which are security related but not events that have to do with anti-terrorist activities. That's a different chapter. This is the only reason I can think of now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Okay. I remind you that when the police line up a group of women and children and babies and shoot them with high-powered weapons, that cannot be classified as anti-terrorist operations. That should be under the heading of serious crime. Did this not -- did the failure of this reporting to mention such a serious crime not cause you to have concern about the information that was being sent up in these documents and the fact that they did not include serious crimes?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information about this crime was received and the service reacted. Why this report does not include that information I cannot explain. I don't know why it is left unmentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Let's move on then to another -- well, before I do, let me ask you, did you see that report, a report of the Podujevo incident, in the report from the SUP for -- that had responsibility or in whose jurisdiction Podujevo fell?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I cannot recall now whether there was such a report.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Did you take any steps against the SUP chief or the OUP chief or the persons in Kosovo who failed to send up in their daily reporting a formal reference to this most gruesome crime?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I must repeat that at that moment, this sort of event was - is something the staff was in charge of. At that time, I had reports from the field where crimes against civilian population were also committed, in the second part of NATO bombing, and reports about heavy damage. Therefore at that point I was tasked by the minister to follow that situation. And this situation down there, whether that had to do with all this activity was for the staff to take care of. Anyway, my attention wasn't focused on drafting paper reports, but I knew of the events. I was informed, and I knew what the OUP in charge and the relevant authority had done. So nobody wanted to conceal the event or slight the consequences or play them down, actually, or I don't know what.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: And I wanted to move on to something else, but you know, again you haven't answered the question. Did you take any disciplinary steps or whatever against the SUP chief or the OUP chief who failed to report this in the reports that were sent on?

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ministry was aware of this event. Both the minister and I were informed about it, and all the measures provided for by the law were taken. At any rate --

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- my attention was directed during this period toward other chiefs of secretariats and not the ones at Kosovo. This applied to the particular event as well. I was in charge of other chiefs of secretariats across Serbia. As for the activities directed toward these secretariats, they were discharged by others who were responsible to the minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: So your answer is no, you did nothing in respect of these people who didn't report it in the formal reporting.

utterances.speaker: VLASTIMIR DJORDJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The -- what happened was not covered up. It wasn't hushed up or suppressed. All the competent organs did what they were supposed to do. Now, whether I noticed at the time if this was part of the daily report or not and if I took any disciplinary measures because this was left out of the report, well, really, at that point in time the entire Serbia as aflame. It wasn't one isolated event. It was a disastrous crime, but you have to understand that half of Serbia was set alight at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Very well. I don't -- I wanted to move on, but I think this might be a convenient time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We have reach the time. Can I inquire again as I did last night, Mr. Stamp?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: I would ask for -- for two sessions, or am I misconstruing the inquiry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: No, you don't usually misconstrue inquiries, Mr. Stamp. You want two session rather than one that we urged on you to finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It has become known to us today that because another trial isn't sitting we can have a courtroom on Monday all day. With that in mind, we will commence at 9.00 on Monday, and we will adjourn for lunch at 12.30 and resume at 1.30 for Mr. Djurdjic's re-examination, and you will just have to finish one way or another by 12.30.

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honours. I'm grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And we will sit, if necessary, until after dark to let Mr. Djurdjic finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. DJURDJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And then you can be a relieved man. I think that way we can be sure of finishing the evidence of the accused rather than him having to hang over the break with the question of evidence continuing. So we will now adjourn to resume at 9.00 on Monday morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 14th day of December, 2009, at 9.00 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 4.07 p.m.,
